# Chinese RSA 

Whoops I've accidentally re-used the same values of e to encrypt my messages, surely that can't have any problems with it right? 

```
c1 = 383959923261929119807038368007402205817644876672712648704618871543676316
n1 = 1481162781400309006761410131097650867404271858439557572357702716476911109
c2 =  148209684408489840089982879211741755329442835437440763430482279534770741
n2 = 1492537926363426731019020977442730849918588087270382126848346266048205229
c3 = 378884813501413942196202692281239732986118950865806779118392938645578756
n3 = 1076853053248773047366157637716823489548111430487584892892366710220262883
e = 3
```

Author: Victor

## Solution

Use [Hastad's broadcast attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coppersmith%27s_attack#H%C3%A5stad's_broadcast_attack).

```python
from sympy.ntheory.modular import crt
from Crypto.Util.number import long_to_bytes
from sympy import integer_nthroot
c1 = 383959923261929119807038368007402205817644876672712648704618871543676316
n1 = 1481162781400309006761410131097650867404271858439557572357702716476911109
c2 =  148209684408489840089982879211741755329442835437440763430482279534770741
n2 = 1492537926363426731019020977442730849918588087270382126848346266048205229
c3 = 378884813501413942196202692281239732986118950865806779118392938645578756
n3 = 1076853053248773047366157637716823489548111430487584892892366710220262883
mods = [n1, n2, n3]
cs = [c1, c2, c3]
c, m = crt(mods, cs)
res = integer_nthroot(int(c), 3)
print(long_to_bytes(res[0]))
```
